national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has left for his four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic this morning. In his departure statement, Mr Modi expressed confidence that his visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia and deepen the civilisational connection with the region. He said that in recent years, the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership has seen significant advancement. The Prime Minister said that he is looking forward to having discussions with the President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, on further deepening cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, and energy, and on advancing the shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan. Mr Modi said that he will also visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, which is a tribute to the close cultural and people-to-people ties that bind the two countries. The Prime Minister said that at the invitation of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, Sadyr Zhaparov, he will travel to Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Summit. Mr Modi said that he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in the neighbourhood and beyond. The Prime Minister said that during his visit to the Kyrgyz Republic, he will also meet President Zhaparov and other SCO leaders and will attend the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 188 Nepal flash floods: Search and rescue operations is on across affected districts of Himalayan nation
national_raw_news.content: The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal and Tibet has risen to 626 this morning, with over 2000 people remaining missing. Police have recovered 233 bodies in Chitwan, 158 in Nawalparasi East, 48 in Gorkha, 47 in Nawalparasi West, 45 in Dhading, 41 in Nuwakot, 31 in Tanahun and 13 in Rasuwa. Search and rescue operations are underway across the affected districts of the Himalayan nation. Officials said that the police are coordinating with residents and other agencies to locate missing people and assist those stranded by the floods. Rescued people are being taken from high-risk areas to safer locations. Additionally, the search and rescue officials are working to clear roads blocked by flood debris and landslides to reopen access and facilitate relief operations. The Ministry of External Affairs yesterday said that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable or are reportedly missing following the flash flood tragedy on Wednesday. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, around 100 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities also remain uncontactable. Addressing the media in New Delhi, Mr Jaiswal said that 63 Indian nationals working at Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project were rescued from the affected area. Mr Jaiswal said that on the Chinese side, around 400 Indian nationals are safe and in contact with their families. Mr Jaiswal said that the government has set up a control room in the Ministry of External Affairs, which is working round the clock. He said, Indian embassies, both in Kathmandu and Beijing, have also set up 24 X 7 helplines. The facility has been set up to coordinate rescue, relief, and tracking efforts for Indian nationals affected by the disaster. Citizens seeking information or assistance can contact the MEA Control Room via telephone (+91 11 2308 8718, +91 11 2308 8719, +91 11 2301 2113), WhatsApp (+91 9968291988), or email(situationroom@mea.gov.in). The ministry is alslo maintaining round-the-clock coordination through dedicated emergency contact lines operated by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu (+977 985 131 6807, +977 970 910 7500, +977 981 032 6117) and the Embassy of India in Beijing (+86 18514284905). The massive flash flood that struck Nepal’s Rasuwa on Wednesday originated in the Tibetan region of China. It swept through the transboundary Bhote Koshi River, leaving a trail of destruction in the country.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 45 National Sports Day being observed today; Prime Minister Modi pays tribute to Major Dhyan Chand
national_raw_news.content: National Sports Day is being celebrated across the country today to commemorate the birth anniversary of one of India’s greatest sporting icons, Major Dhyan Chand. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid homage to the Indian Hockey Legend Major Dhyan Chand on the occasion of National Sports Day. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Major Dhyan Chand’s brilliance in Indian hockey continues to inspire generations. Extending his greetings to all sports lovers, the Prime Minister said that their dedication, passion and determination make the nation proud. The day celebrates India’s rich sporting heritage and encourages people to make sports a regular part of their daily lives. National Sports Day 2026 is being observed as a three-day nationwide campaign under the pillars of Tribute, Play and Move. This year, National Sports Day is being celebrated under the call, Ek Ghanta Khel Ke Maidan Mein”. Various sporting activities are being organised across the country to mark the occasion. In Delhi, Union Ministers Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Arjun Ram Meghwal participated in a cricket match under the campaign. Talking to the media, Dr Mandaviya called upon people to spend at least one hour on the playing field every week to remain fit and healthy. He said a fit youth and a healthy society are essential for building a prosperous nation. Mr Meghwal said he plays badminton every day. He said sports help people remain healthy and fit and also help in keeping stress away. The government has been making sustained investments in India’s sporting ecosystem, with the results increasingly visible on the global stage. India’s performances at major international sporting events reflect the country’s growing strength across Olympic, Paralympic and multi-sport disciplines. In the Union Budget 2026-27, over 4400 crore rupees were allocated to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, compared to just around 1200 crore rupees in 2013-14. India’s Olympic journey has witnessed a significant transformation in recent years. The country won two medals at Rio 2016, seven at Tokyo 2020 and six medals at Paris 2024. India’s performance at the Paralympic Games has also improved remarkably. The medal tally rose from four at Rio 2016 to 19 at Tokyo 2020. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best-ever Paralympic performance with 29 medals. India has also consistently improved its performance at the Asian Games. The country won 57 medals at the 2014 Asian Games and improved its tally to 69 in 2018 and scripted history by winning a record 107 medals in 2023. Initiatives such as Khelo India, the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, and Khelo India Rising Talent Identification are strengthening the sporting ecosystem and helping athletes prepare for competition at the highest level.

national_raw_news.title: Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry clarifies CBG framework under GOBARdhan designed to provide stable price to CBG producers 2 hours ago 43
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has clarified that the revised pricing framework for Compressed Biogas (CBG) under the GOBARdhan Scheme has been designed to provide a stable and viable price to CBG producers while ensuring that consumers do not face any material increase in CNG and household PNG prices. According to a recent newspaper article, the revised price of Compressed Biogas (CBG) under the GOBARdhan Scheme could place a significant additional burden on CNG and household PNG consumers. However, the Ministry explained that this conclusion does not present the correct picture, as it does not account for the Government’s affordability support and the substantially wider domestic gas pool over which the net cost of CBG will now be distributed. The Ministry explained that under the existing system, the procurement price paid to CBG producers is approximately 1 thousand 478 rupees per Million British thermal units, while the revised procurement price under the GOBARdhan Scheme is 2,110 rupees per Million British thermal units. It noted that the Government will also provide affordability support of 10 rupees per kilogram of CBG, equivalent to around 215 rupees per Million British thermal units with 95 per cent methane content, reducing the effective cost to approximately 1,895 rupees per Million British thermal units. Additionally, CBG will be pooled with other domestically produced natural gas, with its net cost spread across a significantly larger domestic gas pool, approximately 2.5 to 3 times the earlier base. The Ministry highlighted that this wider pooling mechanism will substantially minimise the impact on individual CNG and household PNG consumers. The Ministry further emphasized that the revised pricing framework has been carefully designed to balance two key objectives. These include ensuring a stable and viable price for CBG producers to enable sustainable plant operations, while Government-funded affordability support and a substantially wider gas pool protect consumers from any material impact on prices.

national_raw_news.title: Telangana Deputy CM directs Singareni officials to explore joint venture with Karnataka’s Hatti for future gold mining projects 4 hours ago 45
national_raw_news.content: Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka has directed Singareni officials to explore a joint venture with Karnataka’s Hatti Gold Mines for future gold mining projects. He gave these instructions during a visit to the Hatti and UTI gold mines in Raichur district, Karnataka, on the second day of his tour to the region. The Deputy CM, who also holds the Finance and Energy portfolios, said combining the technical expertise of both public sector companies could improve India’s domestic gold production. He noted that Hatti Gold Mines has vast experience in gold exploration, mining, processing and refining, and suggested that Singareni’s technical skills in coal and mineral mining be combined with this experience. Bhatti Vikramarka said gold plays a key role in the country’s economic security, and government companies like Singareni should take the lead in scientifically exploring domestic gold reserves to reduce import dependence. During the visit, he inspected the production unit, mineral processing centre and electro-winning unit at Hatti Gold Mines. Officials told him the project currently produces two to four kilograms of gold daily. He also visited the UTI open-cast and underground gold mines, and asked officials about mining technology, transport and worker safety. Singareni CMD Dr Buddha Prakash Jyothi and other senior officials accompanied him on the tour.

national_raw_news.title: 3rd Vande Bharat train between Jammu and Srinagar will be launched soon: Jitendra Singh 5 hours ago 67
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr Jitendra Singh, said that the third Vande Bharat train between Jammu and Srinagar will be launched soon, terming it a major development for the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that in a video message, Dr Singh said that the Ministry of Railways has also approved a halt at Udhampur following a demand raised by the public. He said the approval for the Udhampur halt was particularly significant, as it was earlier believed that a stop there would not be feasible. Singh also thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Ministry of Railways and the Railway Minister for the development. Reflecting on the expansion of the railway network in Jammu and Kashmir, Singh said that when the Jammu railway station was established in 1972, it took nearly five decades for the railway network to advance further into the region. He said the expansion gained momentum after Narendra Modi became Prime Minister, with railway connectivity extended to Kathua and subsequently to Udhampur and the Kashmir Valley. Singh further said that railway connectivity to the Kashmir Valley was once considered difficult because of the mountainous terrain, but the project was completed despite several challenges. He also highlighted the construction of the world’s highest railway bridge over the Chenab River in Reasi as a major engineering achievement. He said the railway journey has also emerged as an attraction for tourists, with many visitors travelling by train from Jammu to Srinagar to experience the scenic beauty along the route.
